results.summary: This project is a naive 8-bit binary counter built from eight chained D flip-flops that count the clock input. Its eight outputs drive the segments and dot of a 7-segment display, and it lacks features such as a deterministic initial state or a reset. It was constructed during the Hackaday Supercon 2023 ASIC workshop as a rapid learning exercise. Testing consists of pulsing the clock and monitoring the outputs for the binary value, and silicon testers report it counts correctly.

Its pins match the Tiny VGA and TT Audio pinouts, with uo[0..7] carrying RGB, vsync and hsync and uio[7] providing a PWM output. results.summary: This project is a ternary matrix multiplication processor using carry-save adders, written in Verilog. It loads weights into an internal register array and multiplies input vectors by those weights, summing the products to produce 8-bit integer outputs. The datapath is pipelined so it can accept new input vectors while computing on previous ones, producing continuous results. Testing is done by driving the inputs from an external MCU such as a Raspberry Pi over GPIO, and no silicon test reports are available.

results.summary_before: This project implements a programmable sequencer that can generate a sequence of events. It is designed for educational purposes and demonstrates a simple state machine. The sequencer can be programmed via a serial interface and outputs a pattern on the output pins. It is tested by loading a sequence and observing the output.
results.summary: This project is a purely combinatorial generative VGA video synthesizer written in Verilog that renders procedural art at 640x480 and 60Hz. It uses a custom VGA sync engine and screen-space coordinates, relying on bitwise operations and triangle waves instead of RAM or DSP blocks, with a frame counter driving animation over time. A multiplexer selects one of six art engines based on input pins, with a strict priority where ui_in[4] overrides the lower inputs. Testing requires a 25.175 MHz clock and a Tiny VGA PMOD or equivalent resistor-ladder DAC connected to a 640x480 monitor, with DIP switches or buttons on ui_in[4:0] to change modes. No silicon test reports are available.
